notes.title: Neutral, Hostile creatures and Dwellings
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, Lords![/h1][p] [/p][p]We've already talked about factions, so now it's time to introduce some of the [b]Neutral Creatures[/b] and [b]Dwellings[/b] you'll encounter in [i]Lords of the Void[/i].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/033383b05d82692c50957cfd2f8e53f353345da5.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The Calamity transformed many living beings, mutating them into fearsome monsters and beasts. Their symbol (above) is a [b]Patatuf hand holding a club[/b]. The Patatuf is our post-Calamity ogre-like creature — the very first one we designed and fully sculpted in clay.[/p][p][/p][h2]Neutral Creatures[/h2][p][i]Lords of the Void[/i] currently features [b]16 Neutral creatures[/b], with more possibly coming during Early Access. I’ve worked hard to make each one [b]unique and impactful[/b] to gameplay.[/p][p]Yes — even though they're Neutral, [b]it's highly recommended to hire them[/b] for your army![/p][p][/p][p]In the Demo version, you can meet:[/p][list][*][p][b]Patatuf[/b] (Warrior) - a massive ogre-like brute who smashes everything in his path. Tons of hitpoints and high damage, but there's a twist: [b]he’s a fool[/b]. He ignores orders — even if hired, you [b]can’t control him[/b]![/p][/*][*][p][b]Mare[/b] (Warrior) - a life-draining monster disguised as a beautiful woman. Don’t be fooled! Behind the illusion lies a [b]nightmare full of fangs[/b].[/p][p]She’s a strong melee unit who can [b]teleport[/b] and [b]drain life[/b] to heal herself or the weakest nearby ally.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Anurar[/b] (Barrier) - a toxic frog. Like all Barriers, it [b]can’t attack[/b], but it has a powerful ability: a [b]devastating explosion[/b] dealing [b]200 damage that ignores armors[/b]. Extremely effective against most units.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Kobold[/b] (Shooter) - a member of a primitive tribe. Fast, with the [b]Quick Move[/b] ability that lets him move and shoot again. He can also [b]summon allies[/b], so be careful — fight one group, and it might [b]double in size[/b]![/p][/*][*][p][b]Sorcerer[/b] (Magician) - a dark, mutated spellcaster. Can cast:[/p][list][*][p][b]Cursed Bolt[/b] – if it kills, it summons an [b]Imp[/b] at the target's location.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Death Call[/b] – deals damage to [b]all units[/b] on the battlefield.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Imp[/b] (Warrior) - weakest creature in the game. No skills, no special powers. You can find them for free in the [b]Imp Spire[/b] on the world map.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/cd7d1e0ef151f0416c75f6fec49e968f90cdd050.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]There are [b]7 more Neutral creatures[/b] in the Demo, but they’re rarer — I’ll leave them as a surprise. Want to find out what they are? Just play the Demo! 😊[/p][p][/p][p]In the Early Access version we have 3 next creatures:[/p][list][*][p][b]Infegus[/b] (Barrier) - even mushrooms weren’t spared by the Calamity. Infegus is a [b]mutated fungus[/b] that spreads [b]deadly spores[/b] damaging enemies in its area. Like all Barriers, it can’t attack, and this one [b]can’t move either[/b] — so place it wisely before battle starts.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mystic[/b] (Magician) - A deranged, mutated sorcerer. He can [b]steal positive effects[/b] from enemies and give them to allies. His spells:[/p][list][*][p][b]Teleport[/b] a friendly unit anywhere.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Blast[/b] enemies around a target with AoE damage.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Charac[/b] (Shooter) - a mysterious insectoid that spits [b]slowing venom[/b] at its targets. Little is known about them. They appear at the end of the last campaign, and their true power remains a mystery.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/4d95906531118903a1bf7f4fbc011d6dddd6a159.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]As you can see, I’ve done my best to avoid the feeling of “just another shooter” or “just another tank.” Every Neutral unit has a [b]distinct personality and purpose[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][b]Strategies & Combos[/b][/p][p]Build your best team compositions and experiment with powerful combos! For example:[/p][list][*][p][b]Double Patatuf’s damage[/b] with a Paladin’s [i]Bless[/i] ability.[/p][/*][*][p]Use [i]Protection[/i] on [b]Anurar[/b] so it survives its self-detonate ability.[/p][/*][*][p]Combine [b]Infegus[/b] with [i]Stasis Elixir[/i] to boost armor while his spores damage enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]Enhance [b]Mare’s life drain[/b] with [b]Kupala’s healing aura[/b] to keep her sustained.[/p][/*][/list][p]These are just a few of my ideas — I’m excited to see the strategies [b]you[/b] come up with to break the game![/p][p][/p][h2]Dwellings[/h2][p]This is a Dwelling:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/5947e5ece884ec0eda96e2b47774e91b6eae9f26.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]If it has a [b]dark gray banner[/b] like this:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/99459149b3455498da53fdd9cf67405082860295.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]…it means it’s [b]Hostile[/b]. New creatures will continue spawning there and may [b]leave to attack players[/b] or even [b]build new Dwellings[/b]. Don’t wait too long to deal with them — or you might find yourself [b]surrounded by aggressive monsters[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]After conquering a Dwelling, you can choose:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/9aac7f1824047c9762d3c6c6feff02364a99dd73.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Pacify and leave [/b]– the creature becomes recruitable for your faction. Just build a [b]Watchtower[/b] or [b]Town[/b] nearby to control Province with the Dwelling.[/p][p][b]Destroy[/b] – permanently removes the Dwelling and grants you [b]resources[/b].[/p][p][/p][h2]Hostile[/h2][p]Creatures from Dwellings are [b]Hostile to all players[/b]. They’ll attack at every opportunity.[/p][p]Some Hostile teams may be [b]Passive[/b] (not moving). These are placed by the Map Editor.[/p][p][b]Diplomacy won’t work[/b] on Hostile teams.[/p][p][/p][h2]Diplomacy[/h2][p]Diplomacy lets you [b]recruit[/b] or [b]dismiss[/b] Neutral (non-Hostile) units.
Note: It [b]doesn’t work on teams led by a Hero[/b].
Requires at least [b]Level 1 Palace[/b] built in your Capital.[/p][p]Everything you need to know is explained in the UI panel:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/264f1c34c508da9f286ff16fe752a01351a025d4.png"][/img][/p][h2]Early Access Update[/h2][p]The [b]campaigns are basically done![/b]
They’re still undergoing a bit more testing, but I expect that to finish within a month or two.[/p][p]There are [b]four campaigns[/b], each with [b]five missions[/b], full of deep storylines and memorable characters. I’ve worked hard to make sure [b]every mission feels fresh and unique[/b].[/p][p]So if you enjoy [b]strong narratives[/b] and [b]creative[/b] [b]mission design[/b], you’ll likely have a great time finishing the campaigns in [i]Lords of the Void[/i]![/p][p][/p][p]Take care!
— Mateusz from Boargames[/p]

notes.title: Nest - Faction presentation
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, Lords![/h1][p] [/p][p]The last presentation and the final faction of this game: [b]Nest[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/14007a588618595117c011d1a77137949c649420.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The people of the [b]Nest[/b] are lizards who believe that during the Calamity, they were saved from annihilation by a divine [b]Dragon God[/b]. After delivering them from destruction, this Dragon became their ruler — their sacred [b]Dragon Emperor[/b].[/p][p]Symbol of the Nest (above) is the image of the Dragon Emperor himself, depicted as envisioned by the lizard people.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="xVmkhj51_JM;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h2]Lore overview[/h2][p]Among the people of the [b]Nest[/b], there is an unshakable belief in the power of their ruler—the [b]Dragon Emperor[/b]. It was by his might that they were saved from destruction, and by his wisdom that they achieved the most [b]advanced technology[/b] the world has ever seen.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/2d2b2dee3f1c2422595f8f761e83fd990a14e5ea.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Massive gears, hissing steam, and roaring engines — all are inventions of their divine leader. Science and innovation flourish within the empire, where scholars and engineers compete to create ever more powerful devices.[/p][p]Beyond technology, the Nest is defined by its [b]rigid caste system[/b]. A lizard’s role in society depends entirely on its lineage. Even within the military, a soldier’s sub-species determines their function on the battlefield.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/13f200410dbd100622de7cbf2309861aeb638c30.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The Lizard Empire stands as the most powerful faction at the beginning of the [i]Lords of the Void[/i] campaign. Though their laws are strict and merciless, they are undeniably effective, and absolute obedience to the Dragon Emperor fuels both their tireless work ethic and the relentless growth of the state.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/04ab3967fe0c8c7c676bac140f30c7468f782fc5.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]To the lizards, all other factions are mere savages. In their eyes, the others lack valuable technology, discipline, and purpose. They are seen as lazy, disorganized. They are only useful as slaves to serve the glory of the Empire.[/p][p][/p][h2]Campaign hero: Ansa-Ra[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/1abf5f2836d34957bf31ab994436732853d4f079.png"][/img][/p][p][b]The Nest lizards[/b] don't just organize their society by caste. They also pay close attention to lineage. [/p][p]A family name tied to great scientific discoveries or legendary military deeds earns respect across the empire. Members of such noble bloodlines often find it easier to climb the ranks and secure positions of power.[/p][p][/p][p]In the Nest campaign, you’ll follow the story of [b]Ansa of house Ra[/b]. We meet her as she completes her training at the academy. Her ambition? Nothing less than becoming [b]Archlord of the Empire [/b]— the highest authority within the faction, second only to the Dragon Emperor himself.[/p][p]But her path won’t be easy. Her older brother, [b]Ins-Ra[/b], is also vying for the title. He already holds a prestigious role as the [b]Great Officer[/b], commanding the Empire’s military forces.[/p][p]To prove herself, [b]Ansa-Ra[/b] must do more than simply follow orders. She’ll need to show brilliance, initiative, and tactical prowess. After all, in house Ra, there is no room for the untalented.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Units and heroes[/h2][p][b]Units[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Crossbowman [/b]– short, blue-skinned subspecies of lizards is known for its highly developed vision, an evolutionary trait that earned them the role of [b]shooter[/b] within the Nest’s army. Despite their small stature, they are precise, efficient, and deadly at range.[/p][p]Crossbow lizards come with two unique abilities:[/p][list][*][p][b]Crippling Shot[/b] – slows the target, making them easier prey for allied units.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Acid bolt shot[/b] – burns the target’s Mana and reduces their Efficiency, disrupting both spellcasters and ranged attackers alike.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Spearman [/b]– tall and agile, these green-scaled lizards are known for their impressive stamina and [b]speed[/b]. Much like the Order's Ftoomans, Spearmen can [b]restrict enemy movement[/b], slowing down any foes who end their turn adjacent to them. Position them wisely to block advances and protect more vulnerable units.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Alchemist [/b]–[b] [/b]among all the lizards, this subspecies boasts the sharpest minds. While many devote their lives to research far from the battlefield, others take a more active role, becoming [b]Alchemists[/b], battlefield mages who support allies through powerful concoctions.[/p][p]Alchemists don’t cast spells in the traditional sense. Instead, they brew exotic potions to support allied units with [b]temporarily wings[/b], allowing the unit to fly over obstacles. Another elixir emits a protective energy and sets state of [b]Stasis[/b] that [b]heavily increases armor[/b] of targeted unit. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Harpooner [/b]– these huge lizards possess the raw strength needed to wield one of Nest's most devastating inventions — a heavy [b]harpoon launcher[/b] powered by a volatile steam mechanism. This remarkable piece of engineering was personally designed by the Dragon Emperor himself, and it transforms brute force into deadly precision.

The Harpooner stands out as the [b]most Efficient ranged unit[/b] in the game. Thanks to their advanced weaponry, their attacks suffer [b]no damage falloff[/b], hitting with full power at every range.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Wyrm [/b]– a venomous, winged serpents were once doomed to extinction, twisted victims of a cruel mutation. Their fate changed when the Dragon Emperor intervened, using one of his arcane inventions to [b]preserve their lives[/b] and repurpose them for war.[/p][p]In the Nest’s army, Wyrms serve as [b]slow-moving flying units[/b] that excel at [b]poisoning enemies[/b] with attacks. Once per battle, a Wyrm can unleash a [b]devastating acid breath[/b], dealing area damage. [/p][/*][/list][p]Units in total: [b]2 Shooters, 2 Warriors[/b] and [b]1 Magician[/b].[/p][p]All Nest's unit has [b]hitpoints regenerations[/b], a passive ability that restores small amount of hitpoints an the beginning of every action.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/c558606c1e700e1935c94f07e8003fbf9fab2ed1.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/804cdb9b227595e0e8b05506b7a7b2d595d56481.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/60292357dc40d425acf165de30fc9885f58bdf5d.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][b]Heroes[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Officer [/b]– a shooter Harpooner hero, with abilities to give additional action to a allied unit, break armor of enemy unit and to restore all one-time skills as his final ability.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Dragonlord [/b]– a warrior Wyrm hero, with acid breath and venom. He can also cure an allied unit to remove all debuffs.[/p][/*][/list][p]Heroes in total: [b]1 Shooter [/b]and [b]1 Warrior[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Nest's special actions: Investments[/h2][p]Every faction in the game has a set of [b]unique abilities used on a worldmap[/b]. These special actions are unlocked by upgrading the [b]Palace[/b] in your Capital to Level 2 or 3.[/p][p]For the Nest, these are called [b]Investments.[/b] Might be used only once per turn with a costs of small amount of resources.[/p][p][/p][p]Investments list unlocked with Lvl 2 Palace:[/p][list][*][p][b]Workers facility [/b]– builds on a map a facility that [b]increases resources income[/b] from targeted, owned Province.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Field hospital [/b]– builds on a map a hospital on targeted, owned Province. It [b]heals additionally[/b] 25% hitpoints of your units that stands on the same or neighbour Province. [b]This effect is also used on allied teams and units[/b].[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Telescope tower [/b]– builds on a map a tower on targeted, owned Province. The tower gives vision of nearby lands around it.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/23120e45b22cacedaad2cc3a95a6c17c50b023d4.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Investments list unlocked with Lvl 3 Palace:[/p][list][*][p][b]Gold mine [/b]– builds on a map a mine that [b]increases gold income[/b]. Might be built on targeted, owned Province.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Fortifications [/b]– builds on a owned structure (like capital, town or watchtower) on a map. During siege battle, Fortifications provide [b]additional 10 armor points[/b] for every unit in the garrison.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Roads [/b]– builds two parts of road on two tiles on the map. [b]Moving along roads costs fewer movement points[/b] on the map. This [b]applies[/b] to [b]all teams[/b] in the game, [b]including enemy teams[/b], so place roads carefully![/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/286cb2081e55e86eb5c4097a4e63909e34eea447.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]All factions presentations are gone, carry on.[/p][p][/p][p]Take care!
— Mateusz from Boargames[/p]

notes.title: Chrama - Faction presentation
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, Lords![/h1][p] [/p][p]It's time for a first faction from the Early Access release! It's called: [b]Chrama[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/463769853e28ca74047766e301c8e672d013393c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Symbol of the Chrama (above) is a wild forest deity, known to them as the Great Horned One. This mysterious beign replaced the Chrama's people beliefs, not long after the Calamity.[/p][previewyoutube="FL0W-GgpQRM;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]If you like what you are hear please consider following composer of this game - Piotr Hummel. You can find his other great music tracks on his YouTube channel:[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/@piotrhummel"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][/p][h2]Lore overview[/h2][p]Before the Calamity, there were people who stood apart from the other kingdoms.[/p][p]Though the [b]Allmajesty[/b] ruled over them as well, he allowed them to preserve their culture and ancient beliefs. These tribes worshipped gods such as Perun, Tryglaw, Svarozhits, and others tied to fertility, the turning of the seasons, and the eternal cycle of life.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/87055005b156f5aac3bc00006df2b164438cf3bd.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]When the chaos of the Calamity erupted, most of these people lived far from the explosion’s epicenter. Yet the mutating wave of magical energy eventually reached them too. Moss, fungi, and small plants began to grow across their bodies. Their prayers to Kupala for healing went unanswered. As the land around them crumbled into ruin, panic took hold.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/6752ae74524a60d04f31118906522a66b2a0c588.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Something wild awoke within them.[/b]
Their humanity began to fade, replaced by feral instincts and the creeping spread of plant and animal traits. Only fragments of their former selves remained.[/p][p]It was in this moment of desperation that the first [b]Peklenc[/b] appeared—a former elder of the people, now utterly transformed. He revealed to them the [b]Great Horned One[/b], a wrathful god of savage, primal strength. It was he who took them out of their despair.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/20b8257f31873ebae72842c9a0fc4391fb377a35.png"][/img][/p][p]They called themselves the people of [b]Chrama[/b], in memory of the ancient temples —[b]"Chram"[/b]—where they once worshipped their old gods.[/p][p]To this day, they name their warriors after the deities of the past.
Though they now serve a blood-soaked god of fury, they still carry fragments of the world and faith they once knew, before it was shattered.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/efcbbf6b17c852308fee548d23a23e9eb35b4d5e.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p] [/p][h2]Campaign hero: Jutrzenka[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/f4716f647f485ee6af679a982e9f96b569c6dac5.png"][/img][/p][p][b]The people of Chrama are divided into eight clans, each led by a chieftain.[/b]
[b]Jutrzenka[/b] is the leader of the [i]Clan of the Dawn[/i].[/p][p]She is one of the last clan leaders who still dreams of returning to the worship of the old gods. Unlike many of her peers, who are often absorbed in their own interests, Jutrzenka looks beyond, toward the future of Chrama and the wider world. She seeks to forge alliances with the Sphere, hoping to stand united against the rising aggression of the Order.[/p][p]She is willing to make sacrifices for the good of her people.
And while others embrace the brutal power of the [b]Great Horned One[/b] without question, she remains cautious, mistrustful of this wild deity and the changes he brings.[/p][p][/p][p]Her name, [i]Jutrzenka[/i], translates to [b]“Dawn” [/b]— a detail that may carry deeper meaning as the story unfolds.
However, to preserve immersion, names in the English version of the game will remain in their original Polish form. So, while players may meet her in the campaigns, they will come to know her only as [b]Jutrzenka[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Units and heroes[/h2][p][b]Units[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Treemaiden [/b]– a forest wraith that can possess trees on the battlefield. Treemaiden is a [b]barrier[/b], so she can't attack and retaliate. Yet her eerie powers can sow chaos across the battlefield in unique ways.
She has ability summon trees in the battle, which she can later possess, using them to send a storm of leaves that damages a chosen adjacent enemy. Treemaiden can also [b]swap places with a friendly or enemy unit[/b] within her movement range, allowing for strategic repositioning.

Possesing a distant tree can serve not only as a method of attack, but also as an [b]escape[/b], if the situation become too dangerous. In skilled hands, the Treemaiden turns the battlefield into her haunted domain, twisting nature itself to confound her enemies.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Jodut [/b]– the only [b]warrior[/b] among Chrama's ranks. A swift, flying unit bred for the hunt. Its defining trait is[b] Instinct[/b] that gives [b]bonus experience everytime it kills the enemy unit[/b]. 

The Jodut's speed and ability to ignore terrain obstacles make it ideal for [b]hit-and-run tactics[/b], finishing weakened foes, or reaching vulnerable targets deep behind enemy lines. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Kupala [/b]–[b] [/b]another [b]barrier[/b] unit, Kupala is a Chrama's healer with... unconventional twist.
She is an [b]incorporeal spirit[/b], meaning she [b]cannot be killed[/b] in battle.

You might be thinking:
"Wait, what?! An immortal unit? Are you crazy, Mateusz, or what?"

To which I'd respond:
"Quite possibly a valid diagnosis in my case."

So, [b]Kupala is immortal[/b] and [b]she’s a medic[/b].
[b]However![/b] If she stands alone on the battlefield, with all her allies defeated, she will simply [b]fade away[/b], vanishing like morning mist. This mechanic was designed to break the usual “focus-the-healer-first” meta common in other strategy games.[/p][p]Because let’s be honest — if every fight against Chrama boiled down to "kill the healer first," things would get repetitive fast.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Leshy[/b] – probably the most well-known gent from our Slavic lineup. But I gave him a bit of a twist.
Leshy is another [i]barrier unit[/i], a lumbering construct of [b]moss, ferns, and tangled brush [/b]— an entire forest come alive. He’s slow. Painfully slow. But he makes up for it with the ability to [b]teleport to any allied unit[/b], so it’s a good idea to pair him with something fast and mobile.[/p][p]And then there’s his signature move: [b]Fury of nature[/b].
A powerful [b]area-of-effect attack[/b] that brings down nature’s fury on all nearby enemies. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Peklenc[/b] – as a Slavic god of the underworld, [b]Peklenc[/b] punishes the wicked by twisting them into Samojednik - grotesque creatures doomed to feast upon their own flesh.

How could I [i]not[/i] put that guy into the game?[/p][p]Peklenc is [b]Chrama’s only magician[/b], and his spells are as weird as they are powerful.[/p][p]His signature spell, [b]Mutation Bolt[/b], deals damage and then (of course) [b]transforms the target into a Samojednik[/b]. In this form, unit [b]lose all abilities [/b]and [b]can’t use the Wait command[/b]. They [i]can[/i] still perform basic melee attacks, but that’s it. A perfect way to neutralize a high-threat enemy unit, especially one with dangerous special skills.[/p][p]But that’s not all. Peklenc can also [b]drain Mana[/b] from an enemy mage and [b]force a group of enemy units to Wait[/b], pushing them at the end of the combat round.

The English translation of the word [b]Samojednik[/b] is most likely [b]Selfeater[/b] and I think it sounds great![/p][/*][/list][p]Units in total: [b]3 Barriers, 1 Warrior[/b] and [b]1 Magician[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/e8e8040bb1e169977fd593d19bff05afcd9cdf76.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/ec501186745589a57fdc5e681e1e34cd711db737.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/e7a169c8d381b25fe755496c7119af496465fb62.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][b]Heroes[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Sowizrzal [/b]– a magician hero, that shares a spell with Peklenc to transform enemy unit into Samojednik (Selfeater). notes.title: Sphere - Faction presentation
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, Lords![/h1][p] [/p][p]Second playable faction in the campaigns is [b]Sphere[/b]. Let's take a closer look![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/47eef5b099e64e97993083ab3de56022e961daae.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Symbol of the Sphere (above) is a visual of a world exploding, as a result of the Calamity. Although that apocalyptic process has been dramatically slowed down, the image remains on the Sphere’s banners as a constant reminder of what unchecked magic can lead to.[/p][previewyoutube="Zx3jIq1lojY;full"][/previewyoutube][p][b]Fun fact:[/b] This town was entirely sculpted out of air-drying clay by my fiancée, who goes by the nickname KungChan — complete with tiny embedded LEDs. Our original vision was to create the entire game with visuals inspired by [i]The Neverhood[/i], using handmade clay models. However, we quickly realized that this approach was far too time-consuming for a small team like ours, and without the support of a professional studio, the final result just wouldn’t meet the quality we were aiming for.[/p][p]Eventually, we decided to take a different route and looked for an artist who could bring their own visual style to the game. That’s when we found Mr. Szymon — he redrew all the original clay models created by KungChan (including the city, Patatuf, Hound, Phoenix, and a few others) and also crafted the character animations.
A big shoutout to him if he’s reading this! :)[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Lore overview[/h2][p]As the world was crumbling under the overwhelming force of magical energy, a figure known as [b]Aldasir[/b] appeared — a powerful being, perhaps a mage, who managed to slow the collapse. In doing so, he sacrificed his life to preserve what remained and give others a chance to rebuild.[/p][p][/p][p]Not long after the Calamity, a mysterious group calling themselves [b]Aldasir’s Brotherhood[/b] emerged. They seems to try to reconnect the shattered lands and slowly piece them back into a single, unified continent.[/p][p]However, they are rarely seen, and little is truly known about them — adding even more to their mythic presence.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/942ed221ce549c2f988397405c432b8453f44f0f.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Magic itself changed[/b] after the Calamity.
Once orderly and well-defined, split into schools and techniques — it has now become a wild, untamed force. It’s no longer a tool to be wielded, but a raging element that punishes even those who dare to use it.[/p][p]
Out of the four factions, only [b]Sphere [/b]and [b]Chrama[/b] have chosen to continue using post-Calamity magic, but both pay a heavy price for it.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Sphere[/b] mages gradually lose their physical bodies — as if their magic consumes their very existence, turning them into the void.
From the very beginning of their training, they must bind their souls to [b]masks[/b], which serve as vessels for their being. These masks are worn with lightweight cloaks that make movement easier — their only remaining semblance of form.[/p][p][/p][p]There is, however, a second path — one less destructive. In this form of magic, the body remains intact, but it slowly becomes [b]covered in crystalline growths[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/e84031205f70e1c19440146e4a4485093c56538f.png"][/img]The division between these two magical paths is deeply embedded in the Sphere’s rules. Each mage must commit to one path only — a strict rule meant to limit the amount of power any one individual can amass.
This self-imposed restriction serves as a safeguard, meant to prevent any mage from ever becoming powerful enough to trigger another Calamity.[/p][p][/p][p]The Sphere’s ultimate purpose is to [b]understand[/b] and eventually [b]master[/b] this new, chaotic magic.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p] [/p][h2]Campaign hero: Adalbert[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/c2220461f60768b0b46eba24b7ac731a0c2e2388.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Adalbert is a skilled diplomat and Sphere’s foremost envoy when it comes to persuading towns to join their faction. He’s sent ahead to negotiate with independent settlements, building trust and forging connections with their inhabitants.[/p][p]
One such mission is featured in the [b]Tutorial[/b], where you experience firsthand how Adalbert works to win trust.[/p][p]He’s open-minded and pragmatic, even willing to bend the rules if he believes it’s the right thing to do. For Adalbert, principles are important — but not at the cost of missing a crucial opportunity for peace or progress.[/p][p][/p][h2]Units and heroes[/h2][p][b]Units[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Mage [/b]– is a classic offensive spellcaster, capable of dealing powerful [b]single-target magic damage[/b] or weaker attacks to [b]multiple enemies[/b] at once.
In addition to offensive spells, the Mage can also [b]shield an ally[/b] with a protective sphere that absorbs the first incoming hit.[/p][p]Like all magicians, the Mage starts with [b]100 Mana[/b], which is consumed when casting spells.
Each round, [b]10 Mana is restored[/b], but running out of Mana too soon can leave your Mage powerless at a crucial moment.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Sculpture [/b]– a [b]barrier-type unit[/b]. It cannot attack or counterattack. Instead, at the start of its turn, it emits a [b]Decay Aura[/b] that damages all adjacent enemy units.[/p][p]Though immobile in offense, the Sculpture excels in [b]battlefield control[/b] — use it to block chokepoints or protect your more vulnerable allies.
When fighting against a Sculpture, it’s wise to [b]move away[/b] from it as soon as possible, to avoid damage from its lingering aura.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Obelisk [/b]–[b] [/b]a [b]crystal-based ranged unit[/b], slow but durable.
In addition to ranged attacks, it can [b]sacrifice a portion of its own health[/b] to restore Mana to an allied magician — making it a valuable support on magic-heavy teams.[/p][p]Its second ability allows it to [b]regenerate its own health[/b] once per combat, letting it stay alive after it sacrifice some health in exchange for Mana.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Battlemage[/b] – when a Mage falls in battle but their [b]mask remains intact[/b], the Wisemans of the Sphere can transfer the Mage’s consciousness into a magical construct — creating a [b]Battlemage[/b]. This unit wields three spells: to summon Imp, to clone a friendly unit and to create Crystal Blocks on the battlefield (for example: to protect key allies from enemy warriors). 
Once it is out of Mana, the Battlemage can active a final ability: it receives a [b]massive boost to melee damage[/b] for the rest of the battle — at the cost of permanently losing the ability to regain Mana.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Phoenix[/b] – the Sphere’s second [b]ranged unit[/b], but don’t be fooled by the classification, it’s just as deadly in [b]melee combat[/b].[/p][p]When attacking from a distance, the Phoenix [b]ignites itself[/b], conjuring a blazing fireball with a mighty beat of its wings and hurling it toward its target.[/p][p]Its most iconic trait, however, is its ability to [b]rise from the ashes[/b] — once per battle, when slain, the Phoenix will resurrect itself, returning to the fight reborn and ready to strike again[/p][/*][/list][p]Units in total: [b]2 Magicians, 2 Shooters[/b] and [b]1 Barrier[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/c6654b4fc70dc28a7b73ad646939c83df86bd8d0.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/26fc533340c51932f9a964e2d5a5b1e26a421b4a.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][b]Heroes[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Wiseman [/b]– a mage-based hero that follows first path of Sphere's magic. He has an [b]Aura of Power[/b] that increases magical damage for all magicians standing around. A perfect spellcasters leader.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Strategist [/b]– an obelisk-based hero that follows second, crystal, path of Sphere's magic. With his [b]Aura of accuracy[/b], Strategist is a hero dedicated for a team based on ranged units.[/p][/*][/list][p]Heroes in total: [b]1 Magician [/b]and [b]1 Shooter[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Sphere's special actions: Spells[/h2][p]Every faction in the game has a set of [b]unique abilities used on a worldmap[/b]. These special actions are unlocked by upgrading the [b]Palace[/b] in your Capital to Level 2 or 3.[/p][p]For the Sphere, these are called [b]Spells.[/b] Might be used for Mana and Sphere faction has 100 Mana point to spend that way.[/p][p][/p][p]Spells list unlocked with Lvl 2 Palace:[/p][list][*][p][b]Summoning [/b]– creates a portal to remote regions of the world to bring a spectrum. The [b]spectrum[/b] can explore lands, but it cannot lead any units and will be vanished when faces with an enemy. At the beginning of next turn it will be dismissed.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Harvest[/b] – picked controlled Province will produce [b]additional income[/b]. This spell will be auto-used at the beginning of next turn, on the same area.[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Restoration [/b]– heals all your units for 25 hitpoints. [b]This spell can also be used on an allied team[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/1394301aa746bc05bd527fb34d265a4ddfa9d2e3.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Spells list unlocked with Lvl 3 Palace:[/p][list][*][p][b]Haste[/b]– a single targeted team receives [b]two[/b] [b]additional move points[/b].[/p][/*][*][p][b]Return [/b]– targeted team immediately returns to the Capital.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Storm [/b]– deals 30 magical damage to every unit in enemy, targeted, structure (Watchtower, Town or Capital).[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/3e0620af7a0596af1505096cd8beb2fb53833aa5.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]In compare, Order's Decrees are slightly stronger that above Spells. On the other hand, Sphere can use two spells per turn, while Order can use only one Decree.[/p][p][/p][p]This faction is available in [b]Demo[/b]. The last two factions are not, but both will be playable it the [b]Early Access[/b] version.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Coming soon: Chrama faction presentation.[/b]  [/p][p][/p][p]Take care!
— Mateusz from Boargames[/p]

notes.title: Order - Faction presentation
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, Lords![/h1][p]
Each passing day brings us closer to the release of our game in [b]Early Access[/b]. It’s the perfect time to begin introducing the playable factions and shedding more light on the world of [b]Lords of the Void[/b]. [/p][p][/p][p]Today, we focus on one of the central powers in this shattered realm: [b]Order[/b] faction. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/2fbf470e0c87f6392ab4fd8c04d15d7e2e4da4e4.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Symbol of the Order (above) depicts a mighty tower. It's the final bastion of humanity standing against monster and magic.[/p][p]To fully immerse in the spirit of this faction, I recommend listening to their musical theme:  [/p][previewyoutube="HeiltSBblS8;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h2]Lore overview[/h2][p]Long ago, the [b]Allmajesty[/b] united the entire world under a single rule. His reign was absolute, his power unmatched — but even he could not escape the grasp of mortality. As the years wore on, his desperate search for immortality grew ever more extreme, culminating in the casting of the most powerful spell the world had ever known.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/c114b10675714f1ee2132f710eb2a150093dba73.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The unleashed force was cataclysmic. It spiraled beyond control, triggering The [b]Calamity [/b]— a world-ending event that tore the land into floating fragments suspended above the void. Though the collapse of reality has slowed, the decay continues, and all that remains moves ever closer to annihilation.[/p][p]This magical disaster warped every living thing it touched. Nothing remained unchanged. Yet, a sliver of humanity managed to survive. Despite mutations, they endured. From these survivors rose The Order — last bastion of mankind in a world consumed by monsters and ever-twisting magic.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/4c7cb4ebeec3635a90acc0d7c74e2e33f5e6106b.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The Order’s mission is clear: to protect humanity and eradicate all practitioners of magic. This makes them the sworn enemies of the Sphere and Chrama factions. According to the teachings of the Order, only by purging magic from the world can its disintegration be halted.[/p][p]

[/p][h2]Campaign hero: Eiswald[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/9300e8bc69e2e99e93f9196d8e2ee16d073f5ae9.png"][/img][/p][p]Eiswald is a young knight hailing from the modest town of Kalis. Driven by a strong determination, he begins his journey by pledging his loyalty to the Order. Vowing to dedicate his life to defending the world from the monstrous forces that threaten its very existence.[/p][p]His is not a static figure; Eiswald character will evolve throughout the campaign, shaped by the trials he faces and the consequences of the choices he makes. The ideals he clings to at the beginning may not survive the harsh realities of a world unraveling... and neither may he.   [/p][p][/p][h2]Units and heroes[/h2][p][b]Units[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Footman[/b] – a steadfast [b]warrior[/b] trained for both offense and [b]control[/b]. His abilities can stun enemies (that pushes the attacked unit’s action at the end of the combat round) and his presence blocks nearby enemies from reaching more vulnerable units behind the front lines.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Archer[/b] – the only [b]ranged[/b] unit among the Order’s ranks. Might launch an [b]area damage[/b] attack, with reduced damage compared to a single target shot, but it’s highly effective against a large group of enemies, summoned creatures and breaking protecting barriers.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Hound – [/b]a [b]fast-moving[/b], [b]high-damage[/b] unit bred for precision strikes. Deals [b]bonus damage to shooters[/b], making it their natural counter. However, Hounds have [b]low health[/b] so leveling them up might be a real challange. If you achieve that, you will command a fearsome beast, capable of taking out enemy shooters with a single attack.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Cavalier[/b] – a second [b]fast unit[/b] in Order’s ranks. Unlike the Hounds, Cavaliers attacks with crushing [b]charge[/b], [b]dealing damage to the enemy unit and half damage to the target standing next to it[/b]. This ability must be handled with care, because misplaced charges can injure allied units as well.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Templar[/b] – clad in heavy armor, Templars are [b]warriors[/b] granted with parial [b]resistance to magic[/b] (due to his mutation). Through prayer, [b]can boost magic resistance of allied unit[/b]. Using pillum [b]can reach foes at the backline[/b]. Specialized in countering enemy magicians.[/p][/*][/list][p]Units in total: [b]4 Warriors[/b] and [b]1 Shooter[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/2f1358507f45fed17a48f816fa25d41998b97911.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Heroes[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Knight[/b] – a cavalry-based hero focused on speed and aggression. His skills boost unit movement and favor a blitz strategy.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Paladin[/b] – a templar hero built for defense. With his [b]Defensive Aura[/b], he becomes a near-unkillable force as he levels up, shielding allies and holding key positions.[/p][/*][/list][p]Heroes in total: [b]2 Warriors[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Order's special actions: Decrees[/h2][p]Every faction in the game has a set of [b]unique abilities used on a worldmap[/b]. These special actions are unlocked by upgrading the [b]Palace[/b] in your Capital to Level 2 or 3.[/p][p]For the Order, these are called [b]Decrees[/b] and might be used once per turn.[/p][p][/p][p]Decrees list unlocked with Lvl 2 Palace:[/p][list][*][p][b]Scouting[/b] – all Teams and Structures on the map [b]increase[/b] their [b]visibility range[/b] until the end of this turn. [/p][p]Usefull if you are not sure where the opponent is or you wish to search for a glyph on the map.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Economic[/b] – picked Town or Capital will produce [b]additional income[/b] from every Province it controls next turn. This decree will be auto-used at the beginning of next turn, on the same area.[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Medical[/b] – all your units, in every Teams and garrisons, will restore additional [b]15%[/b] of hitpoints at the beginning of your next turn. (basic hitpoints restoration per turn is 10%, with this decree it is increased up to 25%). [b]Allied teams will also be affected by this Decree[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/e18e76711b18546eb9125cf8587d37c68c5d928c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Decrees list unlocked with Lvl 3 Palace:[/p][list][*][p][b]Logistic[/b] – All your Teams gain [b]additional move point[/b].[/p][p]It is recommended to lead few teams, not only one, and this decree gives extra movie point for each of the team. So the more teams, the more beneficial this action becomes.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Training[/b] – Selected Team, that has at least 4 move points, will [b]spend[/b] these [b]move points[/b] on training. All units of that Teams will [b]gain 10 experience points[/b]. [b]Units cannot level up this way[/b].[/p][/*][*][p][b]Plunder[/b] – Selected Team, that stays at enemy Province and has at least 4 move points, will [b]spend[/b] these [b]move points[/b] on plundering. This [b]enemy loses 5 resources from that region and you receives these 5 resources[/b].[/p][p]For now I'm not sure if Plunder is balanced or not, or even if it's usefull in real PvP situations. To this point I played LotV one time with friends on hotseat. Just once, because of lack of time. [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/8840ff77d6f7632fde813e16ab160344f3f5ed54.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This system might be expanded or changed. We'll see what the situation will be after the Early Access release. If there will be some feedback, I probably will react to it.[/p][p][/p][p]This faction is available in [b]Demo[/b] with one story focused mission called [b]Rudrig's quest[/b]. [/p][p]Rudrig is a close friend of Eiswald and he of course takes part in the campaigns.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Coming soon: Sphere faction presentation.[/b]  [/p][p][/p][p]Take care!
— Mateusz from Boargames[/p]

[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/3b1c3f2ad0b92a9ef74fd73afde6a6c5f4b5e13f.png"][/img][/p][p]Welcome Lords!  

Next few small changes and bug fixes.  [/p][p][/p][p][b]Updates[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]every faction can now use one [b]Special Action[/b] on an ally:

I’ll be preparing lore and mechanics presentations for every faction in the game.[/p][p][/p][p]Take care![/p][p]Mateusz from Boargames.[/p]

notes.title: Gameplay update
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, Lords![/h1]

This time, we're rolling out some significant changes designed to enhance the gameplay experience. Here’s the full changelog:
[olist]
[*] [b]A new, concise tutorial[/b]
[*] [b]No more unit limits outside the player’s faction[/b]
[*] [b]Game speed options[/b]
[*] [b]Tooltips for unit statistics[/b]
[*] [b]Screen shake effect for big hits[/b]
[*] [b]Various bug fixes[/b]
[/olist]
Below, I’ve outlined the core details of this update.

[h2]New and Shorter Tutorial[/h2]
The previous tutorial was long and highly detailed, perhaps a bit too much so? :)
I've now created a new, shorter tutorial that focuses on the essentials. With just 10 popups, it highlights the most important aspects of the game. A well-crafted tutorial is key to ensuring players understand the mechanics, and this one should get you up to speed quickly.

You can find the new tutorial here:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/fbe77fdedcfecd09ab4e9a4ea53a52c691911187.png[/img]

[h2]No More Limits on Units Outside of Player’s Faction[/h2]
When I first implemented this restriction, I thought it would provide a more immersive experience, encouraging players to rely mainly on faction units, with just one unit from outside their faction (such as a Neutral monster).
However, after testing and reflection, I now see this was a misguided choice. This game offers a wealth of creatures with unique abilities, and the most enjoyable part is combining these units in creative ways during battles.

So, I’ve decided to remove that limit! Now, team compositions only have two restrictions:
[olist]
[*] You can have a maximum of 3 Elite units
[*] No more than 3 identical units in one team (for example, no more than 3 Footmen)
[/olist]
With this change, you can conquer a Kobold’s Dwelling and recruit up to 3 Kobolds in one team. These creature has the unique ability to summon reinforcements during battle. Now, your Kobolds can call even more Kobolds! Kobolds everywhere!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/86f742cc9a45f82e874eff8a475841a1dfb22f54.png[/img]

Additionally, the Ambassador hero skill, which was previously used to bypass this limit, has been reworked. The new version of this skill reduces the Diplomacy Food cost with Neutral creatures to 0. That means you can recruit Neutral units for free if you have a hero with the Ambassador skill.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/70e9a237419370e3e09dcd8d8a04a0c2c165b77f.png[/img]

[h2]Game Speed Options[/h2]
Is the game running too slowly? Or perhaps too fast? Not anymore.
In the game options menu, you’ll now find an adjustable game speed setting. This allows you to fine-tune the pace of the game to your liking.

Available speed options:
[olist]
[*] 75%
[*] 100%
[*] 125%
[*] 150%
[*] 200%
[*] 250%
[*] 300%
[/olist]
By default, the game will be set to 125%.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/28a151f9b1d5bb7e098350ef4bc8f3ccf6ce7d14.png[/img]

[h2]Tooltips for Unit Statistics[/h2]
I've added a handy new feature to enhance your gameplay experience!
Now, when you open a unit card, you can simply hover your mouse over any statistic you're interested in, and a tooltip will pop up with detailed information.

This also works for checking the current status effects on a unit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/1740ccd3b22989a3b84e0ad95472f7202e908347.png[/img]

Additionally, the bonuses provided by Glyphs or auras are now visible directly on the unit card, giving you a clearer view of how these enhancements affect your units.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/73e31a5054285f11a2c4bd416a9738669f9e3a9c.png[/img]

[h2]Screen Shake Effect[/h2]
To make high-impact hits more satisfying, the screen will now shake slightly whenever a unit deals more than 100 damage with a single attack or area ability. This adds a nice bit of flair, letting you feel the power of your high level heroes and units.
[b]If you’re not a fan of this effect, don’t worry, you can turn it off in the settings.[/b]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
Bugs are a constant challenge, but I’ve squashed several major ones in this update:

[olist]
[*] Fixed an issue with the Charge ability, where it sometimes activated even if the Cavalier or Knight hadn’t moved at least 2 tiles
[*] Resolved a glitch that allowed players to move through the Portal without spending a move point
[*] Academy shows all abilities to buy, even if some units that use these abilities are blocked in the mission (that is mostly important in the campaigns)
[*] Fixed a bug where loading a save would activate all hostile teams on the map, even those that should have remained inactive while waiting in their Dwelling to recruit more units
[/olist]
Several minor bugs also have been addressed.

[h2]What’s Next?[/h2]
Looking ahead, I plan to focus on visual improvements. Perhaps some lighting and shadow enhancements, weather effects, or contrast and color corrections.
As a programmer, I don’t have much experience with visuals, but I’ll give it my best shot. 

That’s all for now. Take care!
— Mateusz from Boargames

notes.title: Heroes of the Void
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, Lords![/h1]

Last week, we discussed the unit classes in the game, and now it’s time to share some insights about the heroes.
The design of heroes in Lords of the Void was guided by two main principles:
[olist]
[*] [b]Breaking the norm of having a single main hero[/b] while maintaining the sense of progress and growing strong.
[*] [b]Ensuring that heroes are intrinsically tied to the faction they belong to[/b], meaning there is no scenario in which a barbarian, for example, becomes a master of magic.[/olist]
In [i]Lords of the Void[/i], heroes continue to level up, enhance their stats, and unlock new talents. However, each hero can be defeated if forced to battle multiple armies in a single turn.

[h2]Hire Many Heroes, Not Just One[/h2]
A player with only a single hero will most likely lose the game. Even if this hero is the most powerful in terms of levels, they will inevitably face attacks from multiple armies, overwhelming them in the process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/d30f4be997890d357a383c3bd079be73a55a4eef.png[/img]

[h2]Synergize Hero Talents with Your Units[/h2]
Do you have heroes in your faction with auras? Consider recruiting units that will benefit most from these abilities.
Does your hero have a spell that paralyzes an enemy unit? Perhaps your strategy should involve including a unit with mana restoration skills, allowing your hero to continuously paralyze powerful foes. There are numerous synergies like this in the game, and leveraging them can be the key to victory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/c187124c6e361b6e61289d5f8f35e8ebdefcd9eb.png[/img]

[h2]Heroes from Other Factions[/h2]
There are special locations in the game known as Ruins, where you might find a Prison with a hero from a different faction than yours. Releasing such hero can introduce new tactical opportunities and catch your opponent off guard. Who knows? There may even be more such locations in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/d2c78681a198bb38320f236e955578f680bfea6f.png[/img]

[h2]An Important Request[/h2]
Outside of the main topic, I have an important request: [b]please share your feedback on the game, even if you haven’t played much[/b]. The game is still in the early stages, even before Early Access, and many of the game’s mechanics are subject to change. This is the perfect time to provide your input if you're interested in a fresh and unique turn-based strategy game.

As a solo developer, managing a project of this scale is challenging. I’m preparing for another round of gameplay and visual improvements, and your opinions would be incredibly valuable. 

Probably a new tutorial will also happen, with a lot less reading :)

That’s all for now. Take care!
— Mateusz from Boargames

notes.title: With a hammer, arrow, spell and skill
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, Lords![/h1]

Welcome to the very first developer's log for [i]Lords of the Void[/i]! Through these logs, we’ll keep you updated on the latest news about the game, including completed features and what we’re currently working on.

It all began with the concept of unit classes. The most common approach in games is to divide units into two categories: melee and ranged. [i]Lords of the Void[/i] takes a different approach, offering four distinct types of units: [b]Warriors[/b] (melee), [b]Shooters[/b] (ranged), [b]Magicians[/b] (spellcasters, as long as they have mana), and [b]Barriers[/b] (units that don’t perform standard attacks but have unique and useful abilities).

[h2]Warriors[/h2]
Warriors are typically the toughest units with the highest health points and damage output. However, they can only engage in close combat. Every unit in [i]Lords of the Void[/i] has its own set of abilities, and mastering their use is key to victory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/0c863a2d972f226a7f627df0c7b644d47fcc9e88.png[/img]

[h2]Shooters[/h2]
Shooters are effective at range, but they deal only half damage in melee combat, so it’s crucial to keep them protected in the backline. A shooter's range stat is essential, as it determines their effectiveness at various distances. Attacks within the unit's range deal full (100%) damage, but if the target is outside that range, the damage is reduced to 60%. Interestingly, if an enemy is within two tiles of a shooter, the damage is significantly increased to 140%!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/61aefb14e3ca54657798ea5915596222aea2ea54.png[/img]

However, shooters cannot attack if an enemy is adjacent to them. The bonus damage is powerful, but positioning is key.

[h2]Magicians[/h2]
Magicians cast spells using mana points. Depending on the type of magician, their spells can deal damage to single or multiple targets, summon creatures, block sections of the battlefield, polymorph enemies, teleport allies, and more. While these abilities are potent, they come with a limitation: mana points. Each spell has a mana cost, and if you’re not careful, your magicians can quickly run out of mana.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/0e2cd2ca9621e69600a9551cc7c5354b282413d0.png[/img]

[h2]Barriers[/h2]
Barriers cannot attack or counterattack, but each one has a unique and valuable ability. Some may explode, damaging all adjacent units. Others can transfer their own hit points to heal an ally, while some can block certain areas of the battlefield or even swap positions with a selected enemy. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443998/4baf2719d30029b47ee1df937b6617f7fc6cfb55.gif[/img]

[b]Leveling Up[/b]
Each unit gains experience from battles and can level up, increasing its hit points and damage by 10%.

In the end, the key to success in [i]Lords of the Void[/i] lies in finding the right combination of units and abilities.

[h2]Are You a Streamer?[/h2]
Do you stream turn-based strategy games, or are you interested in starting? We’d love to have you join the [i]Lords of the Void[/i] community as a streamer! By streaming the game, you’ll be among the first to receive Early Access, and you’ll have an important influence on the development of the game.

Join us on our Discord channel and become [i]Lords of the Void[/i] streamer!

That’s all for now. Take care!
— Mateusz from Boargames
